pros: Free for anyone with a Google account, no seat limits
Native connectors for Google Analytics, Ads, Search Console and Sheets
Sharing and permissions work exactly like Google Drive
BigQuery back end makes it a usable front end for Google Cloud data
Reports embed in websites and intranets with a simple iframe
cons: Blended or Sheets-backed reports get slow and can time out
No shared metrics layer, so definitions drift across reports
Many non-Google sources need paid third party connectors
No alerting and limited chart formatting compared with paid BI tools
starting_price: $9 per user per project per month
verdict_line: Pick Looker Studio if your data lives in Google products and you need shareable dashboards at no cost.

pros: Open source edition is free with no user limit
Question builder lets non-SQL users query tables with filters and summaries
Runs against Postgres, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery and more in minutes
Interactive embedding puts sandboxed analytics inside your own product
Dashboard subscriptions and alerts deliver to email and Slack
cons: No SaaS connectors, data must already sit in a database or warehouse
Chart types and formatting are basic next to Tableau
Sandboxing, SAML SSO and audit logs are paid features
Paid tiers jump in price steps rather than scaling per seat
verdict_line: Pick Metabase if your data is already in a database and you want self-serve dashboards without per-seat licensing.

pros: Compose SDK renders analytics as native React components in your product
ElastiCube models join many messy sources without a warehouse
Data security rules and API automate per-tenant provisioning
Runs managed in the cloud or self-hosted on Linux and Windows
Pulse alerts notify by email, mobile or Slack when KPIs move
cons: Quote-only pricing with no free tier or self-serve purchase
Ad hoc visual exploration is slower than Tableau or Qlik
ElastiCube builds need memory, scheduling and monitoring
Roadmap and platform migrations have shifted several times
verdict_line: Pick Sisense if you are a software vendor embedding customer-facing analytics and need developer-grade SDKs.

pros: Associative engine shows excluded values in grey, not just matches
Section access enforces row-level security inside the data model
Load script handles incremental loads and transformations at load time
In-memory engine stays fast on tens of millions of rows
Available as SaaS or client-managed on Windows servers
cons: Set analysis and load script skills take months to learn
Cloud plans carry a monthly minimum, no small-team pricing
Default dashboards look plain without manual formatting
Two deployment models and several licence schemes confuse admins
verdict_line: Pick Qlik Sense if users need to explore across many linked tables and you can staff Qlik developers.

pros: Over a thousand prebuilt connectors to SaaS apps and databases
Magic ETL lets analysts join and clean data without SQL
Mobile apps render dashboards and alerts properly on phones
Personalised data permissions filter every dataset per user
App Studio adds write-back forms and workflows on top of data
cons: Consumption credit pricing is hard to forecast and grows with use
Cloud-only, no self-hosted option for regulated environments
Works best with data copied in, duplicating an existing warehouse
Visual exploration and custom formatting lag Tableau and Qlik
verdict_line: Pick Domo if a business team must connect dozens of SaaS sources and build dashboards without data engineers.
